memos.headline: S04 and S10 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S08, S01, and S02 Remain Structurally Weak
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of June 13. S04 is the standout leader, trading within 0.8% of its 52-week high with RSI at 71.5 and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +17.2%—this is a textbook momentum name, though the elevated RSI and +11.6% extension above the 50-day mean warrant caution on fresh entries. S10 is similarly strong with +20.8% over 12 weeks and +16.6% above its 50-day mean, but the higher ATR (2.90%) and still -5% from highs suggest it has more room to run before getting crowded. On the weak side, S08 is in a persistent downtrend at -24.2% from its high, trading 12.5% below its 200-day mean with negative relative strength across all timeframes—I see no reason to step in front of that. S02's 4-week bounce of +14.3% is eye-catching but the stock is still 50% off its high and 38% below its 200-day mean; this is a dead-cat bounce until proven otherwise, and I'd need to see it reclaim at least the 50-day mean before reconsidering.

views.note: Near 52-week highs with dominant relative strength (+17.2% vs SPY over 12w); would reassess if price breaks below the 50-day mean (~$425).
Strong 12-week momentum (+20.8%) and relative strength (+15.5% vs SPY), with RSI 62.7 leaving room; a close below 130 (roughly the 50-day mean area) would negate.
Persistent downtrend: -24.2% from high, -12.5% below 200-day mean, negative relative strength on every timeframe; no reversal signal yet—would reconsider above 210.
Down 50% from highs and 38% below the 200-day mean; the 4-week +14.3% bounce looks like a bear-market rally—need a sustained move above the 50-day mean to change my view.
Weak RSI at 40.3, below both moving averages, and -10.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks; would need a close above 170 to reconsider.

Decent 4-week momentum (+6.5%) and best 4-week relative strength in the universe (+5.4% vs SPY), but still -15.4% from highs and only +1.8% above 200-day mean—trend is improving but not yet confirmed; a break below 165 would invalidate.
Healthy longer-term trend (+9.6% above 200-day) but 4-week relative strength has turned negative (-2.1% vs SPY), suggesting momentum is fading near-term.
Strong 1-week pop of +7.5% pushed RSI to 68.7 but 12-week relative strength is -8.1% vs SPY; this looks like a mean-reversion bounce rather than a trend change—watching for follow-through.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Margin Expansion; S07 and S09 Show Earnings Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin growers and names where earnings power is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 69.2% YoY revenue growth, a 42.6% net margin, and only $8.46B in total debt—this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 is similarly compelling at 38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth on 12% revenue growth, indicating significant operating leverage. On the other end, S07 posted a -9.8% revenue decline and -29.8% net income drop with $31.74B in debt, which is over 2x its trailing annualized revenue—a leverage profile I'm unwilling to pay for amid shrinking earnings. S09 is flat on revenue (+0.1%) with net income declining 6.2% and a thin 9.3% margin, suggesting no near-term catalyst for re-rating. I would need to see margin stabilization in S07 and S09 before reconsidering.

views.note: 69.2% revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, and minimal leverage ($8.46B debt) make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth on 12% revenue growth signals powerful operating leverage and low debt ($14.79B).
36.9% net margin, 13.3% revenue growth, and 17.7% net income growth with manageable $42.88B debt support a durable earnings profile.
64.2% YoY net income growth is impressive but 11.0% net margin and $58.75B debt leave less room for error; I need to see margin expansion sustain.
Solid 26% net margin but only 5.1% revenue growth and $92.20B in total debt suggest mature, slower compounding.
32.3% net margin is attractive but $407.22B total debt dwarfs the balance sheet; earnings growth of 9.1% is modest relative to that leverage.
9.8% revenue growth is decent but 5.7% net margin and $81.27B debt with unavailable YoY net income comparison limit conviction.
Flat revenue (+0.1%), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin signal cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue down 9.8%, net income down 29.8%, and $31.74B debt on ~$57B annualized revenue is a deteriorating earnings story with uncomfortable leverage.
19.1% net margin is respectable but -2.1% revenue decline and flat net income (+0.4%) suggest stagnation; $24.25B debt is manageable but growth must return.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Benign CPI — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, while CPI is running at just 2.3% y/y and unemployment has drifted up 40bp over the past year to 4.30%. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+90bp y/y to +0.46pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual easing rather than further hikes. The 10y yield at 4.41% is only modestly higher over three months (+14bp), suggesting term premium is contained for now. My base case is a prolonged pause transitioning to cuts later this year if unemployment continues to rise — a regime that favors duration-sensitive growth and defensive staples over pure cyclicals. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment dropping back below 4.0% would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a pause-to-easing regime with contained inflation at 2.3% y/y and a steepening curve.
Defensive staples should outperform as unemployment trends higher (+0.40pp y/y) signaling late-cycle softening.
Banks benefit from a steeper curve (+0.46pp 10y-2y) but rising unemployment and eventual rate cuts compress NIM upside.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a softening labor market and a Fed that has held rates at restrictive levels for an extended period.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst in a slowing-growth, stable-inflation environment; staying neutral until demand signals clarify.
Rate-sensitive sectors gain as the market prices in easing; 10y yield only +14bp over 3m despite sticky policy rate supports valuations.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S10 Positive Momentum vs. S08 and S01 Negative Drift
memos.body: I see a clear sentiment split across the universe based on earnings-season price reactions and subsequent filing cadence. S04 posted a standout +7.6% reaction to its April 30 results and S10 followed with +3.2% on May 28, both suggesting positive narrative momentum that has not yet been diluted by negative follow-on filings. On the other side, S08 dropped -3.7% on its May 1 earnings and has had only a single 'Other Events' filing since, offering no catalyst to reverse the negative tone. S01 also fell -3.7% on Q3 results and has since disclosed a senior officer departure/appointment on June 9, which I read as incremental uncertainty rather than a positive reset. S02 stands out for an unusually high volume of management-change filings (four in six weeks), which signals organizational instability and warrants caution even without an earnings price reaction to anchor on.

views.note: Strong +7.6% earnings reaction with no subsequent negative filings suggests positive sentiment momentum still intact.
Fresh +3.2% earnings beat on May 28 is the most recent positive catalyst in the universe and likely not fully priced.
Negative -3.7% earnings reaction with no positive follow-on narrative; tone remains downward.
Earnings drop of -3.7% compounded by a June 9 officer change filing adds uncertainty rather than recovery signal.
Four officer departure/appointment filings in six weeks signals unusual management churn, a negative sentiment flag.
Mild +1.7% earnings reaction and steady stream of Other Events filings suggest stable-to-positive tone, though conviction is moderate.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and routine filings leave sentiment flat with no clear directional signal.
Negligible +0.4% earnings reaction and only a routine shareholder-vote filing since; no sentiment edge.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Still Elevated; No Clear Geopolitical Catalyst to Differentiate the Universe
memos.body: I see a macro backdrop where the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 27% over the past month to 484.65 but remains roughly 12% above its level three months ago, suggesting the acute phase of policy shock (likely tariff/trade-related) is fading without fully resolving. VIX at 18.02 is down 26% over three months and HY OAS is stable at 3.17%, indicating credit markets are not pricing in imminent geopolitical disruption. WTI at $68.73 is up 8.5% month-over-month, which could reflect either supply-side tightening (OPEC+ discipline, sanctions enforcement) or a modest demand recovery—either way it is not at levels that signal acute energy-security stress. The 8-K filings across the universe are generic 7.01/8.01 items with no disclosed content pointing to sanctions exposure, export-control impacts, or supply-chain restructuring, so I have low conviction differentiating names on geopolitical grounds alone. I would need concrete evidence of China-related revenue concentration, export-license dependencies, or sanctions-adjacent counterparty risk to move off neutral for most of these names.

views.note: Frequent Reg FD filings in June suggest active investor engagement but without disclosed content I cannot assess geopolitical exposure.
Four 8-K filings in three weeks (Apr-May) is unusually high cadence; absent detail on whether these relate to trade-policy impacts, I stay neutral.
Most recent 8-K filed just yesterday (Jun 12) keeps this name on my watchlist, but declining VIX and policy uncertainty argue against a defensive posture.
Only two filings and no geopolitical signal; stable HY spreads suggest no credit-market concern about policy-exposed sectors.
Single 8-K with no detail; WTI recovery and easing uncertainty are mildly supportive but insufficient for a directional call.
One Reg FD filing in early May and no further disclosures; no geopolitical basis to differentiate from the pack.
